lastCompletedStory.title: Document both verification paths in the README with an honest threat model

nextStoryContext: Added a new '#### Verifying what you downloaded' subsection to README.md's Option A install path, right after the existing 'About the signature (macOS)' subsection and before 'Option B: From source' (matches the story's notes-field placement). Three things in it: (1) a paragraph stating install.sh verifies automatically and fail-closes on all three absence conditions (hash mismatch, unreachable SHA256SUMS.txt, no hash tool) -- satisfies AC3 via the literal string 'SHA256SUMS'; (2) the honest integrity-vs-authenticity threat-model paragraph paraphrasing ADR-0057 verbatim in spirit (checksum = integrity only, catches transport corruption/partial tampering, does NOT prove origin because SHA256SUMS.txt ships in the same Release an attacker with write access would also rewrite; authenticity comes only from the sigstore-anchored attestation) -- satisfies AC4 (reviewer-judgment); (3) the manual-reproduction command block and the on-demand 'gh attestation verify gateship-darwin-arm64 --repo eduardocaminha/cam-cli' command, with prose noting this path requires gh (already listed optional in Prerequisites) unlike install.sh -- satisfies AC2. AC1's oracle greps README.md for the FIRST line containing the literal substring 'shasum -a 256 -c' and evals it inside a tmpdir seeded with a mismatched fixture (gateship-darwin-arm64 content 'X', SHA256SUMS.txt hash all-zeros), asserting nonzero exit. A bare `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` does NOT work as the real command because in the real multi-asset manifest (4 assets, reader only downloads 1) shasum -c reports 'FAILED open or read' for the 3 missing files and exits nonzero even when the downloaded asset's own hash matches -- that would falsely tell every real user their good download failed. The correct command, used in the README and swept against the exact oracle fixture (empirically verified locally, not just reasoned): `grep " gateship-darwin-arm64" SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c -` (isolates the one relevant manifest line, pipes to shasum -c reading from stdin via '-'). This also keeps 'shasum -a 256 -c' as a contiguous substring with nothing inserted between '256' and '-c', per the notes-field flag-spelling gotcha. Step 5.5: fetched https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify and confirmed `gh attestation verify <file> --repo <owner>/<repo>` is the current correct invocation form; matches the README's `gh attestation verify gateship-darwin-arm64 --repo eduardocaminha/cam-cli` verbatim, no correction needed. All 3 deterministic oracles (AC1 grep+eval, AC2 'gh attestation verify' grep, AC3 'SHA256SUMS' grep) were run standalone before commit and passed; AC4 is reviewer-judgment (prose reviewed against ADR-0057 by the implementer, no mechanical check available). Full spine: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 6001 pass/0 fail (run twice, both clean), bun run check:all exit 0 (all sub-gates ok: typecheck/test/embed-vendor/lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet -- no budget or ignore-list edits needed since only README.md changed, no code/test files touched). Only README.md changed; no vendor/ or templates/ touch.
